answer.evidence: The ambulance is drawn in side view facing east. The box body has a bright roof band at rows 12-16 (L about 234) above the grey side face at rows 17-41 (L about 180). That is a 5-row top surface on top of a 25-row south face. The cab roof has a similar band at rows 13-16. The band has no distinct edge line or eave shadow, only a tone step at row 17, so the top surface is weaker than in the green references. Row 24 is a horizontal trim line on the side face and is not a top surface. The red stripe, wheels, cross and windshield are details on the front face. The siren lights at rows 10-12 are decor.

styleAnswer.evidence: The ambulance is a white/grey body with a red cross, a few windows and dark wheels. The body reads as roughly 3 lightness steps (white, light grey, grey-blue shade) and the large side panel is a flat white fill with no grain, panel seams, dirt or speckle. The measured 24% near-flat coverage is above every reference (hedge 0%, well 0%, stall 13%). Its 9 visible tones per tile only match the hedge, and are well below the stall (17) and well (20). The outline is tinted (0% neutral dark edges) and sits near the dark material tone, so it is not a sticker line, but the surfaces are shallow. The references show per-material ramps of 5-6 steps with texture dots (hedge leaf clumps, stall wood grain and goods, well stones shaded one by one). Next to them the candidate looks flatter and thinner in shading, with a big plain body, little material texture and few highlights.

styleAnswer.evidence: The ambulance is a white/grey body with a red cross, a darker lower strip and a blue-grey window. It uses about 3 lightness steps on the white body (white, light grey, mid grey) and shows no panel grain, speckle or per-part highlights. The large body areas are near-flat (24% coverage in 5x5 flat blocks, against 0-13% for the richer references such as the stall at 13% and the well and hedge at 0%). At 9 visible tones per 16x16 tile it matches the hedge, but it falls well below the stall (17) and the well (20), which are the closer references for a structured prop. The hedge is a uniform texture with many tonal clusters, while the ambulance is smooth flat panels. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted (blue-grey) and not a black sticker line, which is a plus. Even so, the shading is shallow and the large flat white and grey panels read thinner and more sticker-like than the Beodeul props, which carry 5-6 steps with texture dots.

answer.evidence: The ambulance is drawn in side profile, facing east. Its south face is the grey body, with a red stripe and cross, in rows 17-41 (25 rows). The top of the box body and the cab each carry a bright white roof band at rows 12-16 (L=234 against L=186 for the face below). The band ends at a tonal step at row 17, but there is no 1-row edge line and no eave shadow, so this is a weak top surface. The horizontal crease at row 24 sits inside the side face and is not a roof edge. The silhouette widens gradually from 59 to 90 px over rows 11-30, and this rounded roofline supports a roof plane seen from above. The wheels, stripe and windshield are all front-face detail.

styleAnswer.evidence: The ambulance is a large vehicle prop with a mostly flat white/light-grey body. It has about 3 lightness steps on the body (white, light grey, mid grey-blue) and a small shading ramp on the dark wheels and windows. Measured: 9 visible tones per tile matches the hedge (9) but is well below the stall (17) and well (20). Near-flat coverage is 24%, the highest of all pieces (references 0-13%), which fits the large flat white panels of the body and the red cross area. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted (bluish/dark grey-brown), but it reads as a fairly continuous dark contour around the whole vehicle, which gives a mild sticker look. Texture is limited to a few window reflections, door seams and lights. Beodeul props carry 5-6 steps with grain, speckle and per-element shading, whereas the body here is shallow with large flat panels. Overall it is clean and readable but flatter and shallower than the stall and well references.

styleAnswer.evidence: The ambulance is a vehicle and larger than the references. Its body is a mostly flat white/light-grey with only about 3 steps (white, light grey, mid grey) plus a cool grey-blue window. The red cross and stripe are flat fills. Measured: 9 visible tones per tile is below the richer references (stall 17, well 20) and about equal to the hedge (9), but 24% near-flat coverage is well above every reference (0-13%). The dark edge pixels are tinted (0% neutral), so the outline reads as dark, slightly cool, tinted tones rather than pure black. However, it is applied uniformly around the whole body and wheels, which gives a mild sticker look compared with Beodeul's selective outlines. Texture is limited to a few panel lines, window highlights and wheel details. The body panels are large, flat and lightly shaded, and there is no grain or speckle, unlike the per-stone and per-tile detail on the well and stall. A careful artist would find it flatter than the references.
